record.original_question: Justify the observed tendency of generic two-dimensional Euler flows with small numerical viscosity to approach integrable point-vortex configurations, and design a dissipation model that produces this asymptotic integrable dynamics.

evidence.quote: Problem 27. Justify the phenomenon observed in [103, 105] that integrable cases of point vortices seem to be attractors for 2D Euler flows with generic smooth initial vorticity in 2D (for small numerical viscosity). Design a model of dissipation in the 2D Euler equation which would produce such an integrable dynamics at large times. Historically, studies of point vortices include constructions of explicit solutions, conditions for the presence and absence of a collapse, description of relative equilibria, bifurcation of solutions for N = 2 and N = 3 point vortices, see [1, 114]. A nice collection of integrable motions on the sphere and torus can be found in [104, 114]. For manifolds with boundary there is a broader variety of motions. For instance, the cusp motion of a pair of point vortices on a half-plane is related to the golden ratio [77]. The motion of 3 point vortices on a half-plane is already non-integrable [145], as well as, apparently, the motion of two point vortices in the quadrant. The motion of point vortices on the half-plane and the quadrant for the lake equation is related to the motion of vortex rings, membranes and to the more general binormal equation [62, 63, 145].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equations on a domain $M \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ (e.g., the plane, sphere, torus, or half-plane), written in vorticity form for the scalar vorticity $\omega(x,t)$:
$$\partial_t \omega + (u\cdot
abla)\omega = 0, \qquad u = 
abla^\perp \Delta^{-1}\omega, \qquad 
abla\cdot u = 0,$$
with appropriate boundary/decay conditions. A configuration of $N$ point vortices with strengths $\Gamma_1,\dots,\Gamma_N \in \mathbb{R}$ at positions $z_1(t),\dots,z_N(t) \in M$ evolves according to the Kirchhoff–Helmholtz Hamiltonian system
$$\Gamma_k \dot{z}_k = J\,
abla_{z_k} H(z_1,\dots,z_N), \qquad H = -	frac{1}{2\pi}\sum_{j
eq k} \Gamma_j\Gamma_k G(z_j,z_k),$$
where $G$ is the Green's function of the Laplacian on $M$ and $J$ is the standard symplectic rotation. Such an $N$-vortex system is called integrable when it admits a complete set of independent commuting first integrals (e.g., $N \le 3$ in the plane).

Numerical simulations of 2D Euler flows with smooth generic initial vorticity and small numerical viscosity exhibit long-time concentration of vorticity into a small number of localized blobs whose centers appear to approach motion governed by an integrable point-vortex Hamiltonian.

(a) Provide a rigorous justification of this phenomenon: prove, under suitable hypotheses on initial data and on the regularization, that solutions of the 2D Euler equations (or their slightly viscous counterparts) asymptotically organize into $N$ concentrated vortex regions whose centroids converge in an appropriate sense to trajectories of an integrable $N$-point-vortex system.

(b) Construct an explicit dissipation/regularization mechanism (a modified vorticity equation of the form $\partial_t \omega + (u\cdot
abla)\omega = \mathcal{D}[\omega]$ for some operator $\mathcal{D}$) such that, for generic smooth initial data, the large-time dynamics of the resulting solutions is asymptotically described by an integrable point-vortex Hamiltonian system.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as a research challenge concerning the long-time behavior of 2D Euler flows and their relation to integrable point-vortex systems. No published rigorous justification or canonical dissipation model producing integrable asymptotic point-vortex dynamics appears to be available; related numerical observations exist but the question is widely regarded as open.
